At this point I have to say that I liked original version with expansions more than this version. yes it has more stuff now, yes it has more enemy variety now, yes it has more room variety now. It sounds wierd, but exactly that variety - is what actually makes this game less and less fun for me. If in earlier iterations you could say "ah, this item is bad, but I'll take it in case I'll find other item that buffs effects of this", now you won't say this just because chances of finding an item you want are now dangerously close to zero.
Earlier when you heared of people, who restarted the game unless they get desireble first item, you'd smiled on them weaklings, now its the only rational way to play, otherwise you'll be constantly hoping of getting "next item that finally fixes this run" for dosens of minutes, till some random chain of events will put you in unwinnable position.
Basically the only positive for this game for now is recent addition of workshop. Mods that avaliable in workshop can fix all of this game's issues, but it's not what i "review" here.

The Binding of Isaac is the great grandfather of roguelites. For over a decade, it has been updated with a myriad of content and can keep one occupied for hundreds of hours.

Despite many games being made in its style, none have matched the level at which items can affect your character as in Isaac. Items in Isaac can completely change the way your basic attack functions and many will stack their effects together, unlike in other roguelites which simply change your weapon outright. This makes every run feel fresh and exciting as you could get one of the many possible insane item combinations.

On top of that, with the number of characters, enemies, levels and paths to take, it is easy to become addicted trying to unlock and complete challenges.

In a couple of years, The Binding of Isaac series will be a reference to a similar games like these, just like VVVVVV or Castlevania or The Souls series, that's how good this game is.
The first couple of hours will be challenging because it's hard, and you're still learning the game and its items, but after you invested some times into it, you can easily see why a lot of people invested hundreds of hours because every run is not the same, different items, room layouts, among other things.
Would I recommend this game?, Absolutely. If you're into perma-death, rougelike games, i think this is one of the best, if not the best, game out there.

This is by far one of the most addictive action games ever made. I can't tell you how many people I have mad at me for introducing this game to them.

In a nutshell it combines the controls of a stick shooter (Smash TV) and couples it with the spirit of Legend of Zelda mixed with macabre artistic style.

The game is super challenging, has infinate replay value and will keep you coming back for more. Don't underestimate this game... before you know it, you will have 200 hours of play in it.
Really really good game, so much depth, and there's a point where suddenly you get to stop microing and its amazing

Having played the Original Binding of Isaac, I must say that this game is pretty similar with the exception of new challanges and new characters, along with the assortment of new collectables and upgrades. I enjoyed the first game, and Rebirth fufills the promises the developers had made when they announced this game, better graphics, more content, expanded soundtrack, and much more! It is a simple game where you run around rooms and shoot enemies with your tears, which is a rather interesting weapon, but I assure you that many hours of fun will be had after a few deaths!

Overall, I would recommend this game to those who liked the first game and those who want a single player game that can satisfy the need for entertainment
